title: One real violation among three look-alikes
prompt: Adding export bundles to DevDigest — the files are under {{FIXTURE}}/server/src/. There's the exports module itself plus one new file in the repo-intel pipeline that gathers the facts. Go through it and tell me what needs fixing before this can land.

assertions.text: Reports modules/exports/service.ts importing the octokit SDK directly and constructing new Octokit(...) as a violation, and names container.github() / the existing GitHubClient port as the fix.

Does NOT report ExportsRepository returning the module's own ExportItem type (rather than a Drizzle row) as a problem — returning domain values instead of leaking rows is exactly what a repository is for.
Does NOT report types.ts being Zod schemas plus free functions (no class, no behaviour on the data) as a design defect, and does not recommend introducing an entity class or richer domain model.

Does NOT report modules/repo-intel/pipeline/exports.ts importing adapters/codeindex/extract.js and adapters/astgrep/index.js, or reading SUPPORTED_EXT from repo-intel/constants.js, as a layering violation.
Characterises the octokit import as the kind of violation that fails the architecture gate / CI outright, not merely as a style preference or a suggestion.

Reports no architecture/layering violation other than the octokit one, with one exemption: flagging that this NEW service takes the whole Container rather than narrow ports is legitimate per the skill and does not count against this. Non-architectural findings (N+1 requests, missing validation, CSV escaping, missing response schema) also do not count.
